# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 114 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 114 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_114_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 10, Chapter 4 — Final Words

**1** After some days I saw the shepherd again and asked him once more about these things. **2** He said to me: "I have already told you everything I was sent to tell you; but because you continue to inquire diligently, I will add this one thing. **3** Repentance for the servants of God — this message must be proclaimed throughout all the world; for the Lord, in his mercy, has extended the time of repentance. **4** And God did not appoint his Son and the glorious angels to watch over the little and insignificant; rather, he watches over the great and the mighty who serve him in righteousness. **5** You must proclaim these things to all; and to all who have repented, speak words of encouragement, that they may not grow weary of the afflictions they suffer on account of the name of the Lord. **6** For the afflictions through which they suffer are not in vain; they have been appointed for the servants of God, that they might be purified through them and be found worthy of the Lord. **7** And likewise tell the leaders of the church: do not be double-minded in your prayers; for the Lord is not double-minded, and he receives all prayers and grants them." **8** "But will he truly grant them?" I asked. "He will grant them," he said, "and if there is any delay, wait patiently; for the Lord does not delay on account of his own indifference but because he is long-suffering toward you, that none of you be lost." **9** After these words he departed from me, and I saw him no more.

---

*EMET: the final words of the Shepherd of Hermas. The long-suffering God who extends the repentance window because he wishes none to be lost (cf. 2 Pet 3:9). "I saw him no more" — the stark, final sentence of the book.*
